title: Gym Days and the Loc Styles That Keep Up
description: i started paying attention to how black women show up to the gym and i haven't stopped since. there is a whole unspoken architecture to it — the way loc styles get pinned and wrapped and secured before a workout like a ritual before a ritual. i used to think the gym was just functional. then i started noticing the details. in #Atlanta fitness spaces in #LosAngeles outdoor gyms everywhere i've traveled — black women have turned the practical question of what to do with locs into something quietly artistic. hairstyles that survive a full session and still look intentional on the other side. that's not an accident. that's mastery dressed up as routine.
alt_text: A Black woman with thick mid-length locs secured in a high puff with a silk-lined scrunchie mid-workout in a bright modern gym setting focused expression and confident athletic stance.

title: What the Gym Taught Me About Protecting My Locs
description: there's a discipline to it that i respect deeply. black women who have locs and train seriously have figured out something the wellness industry took forever to acknowledge — that protective styling and physical performance are not in conflict. they never were. i've been in gym spaces from #Miami to #Chicago and the loc styles i observe before a lifting session or a run are as considered as anything i've seen on a runway. a good braid-out tuck. a loc bun that doesn't shift. wraps that stay through sweat and still look like a choice. hairstyles built for endurance. the gym is just another place black women have had to innovate without being asked and then watched the world catch up slowly.
alt_text: Overhead flat lay of gym essentials — water bottle resistance bands and a silk scarf — arranged alongside a photo of a Black woman's neatly wrapped loc bun ready for a workout session.

title: Locs at the Gym — More Than a Hairstyle Choice
description: i've been thinking about the quiet negotiations black women make every single day. the gym is one of those spaces where those negotiations become visible if you know how to look. loc styles adapted for movement. hairstyles that protect the hair through sweat and friction without sacrificing the identity woven into every strand. i watched a woman in a #Brooklyn gym spend four minutes perfectly pinning her locs before a deadlift session and i thought — that's not vanity that's knowledge. the kind passed down and figured out and refined over time. #BlackWomenWhoLift carry so much more than weight in those spaces. and their locs carry the whole story.
alt_text: A close-up side profile of a Black woman with long styled locs pulled into a sleek high bun secured with a gold cuff wearing athletic wear in a softly lit gym environment with weights visible in the background.

title: What the Ocean Keeps Trying to Tell Me
description: i've been collecting shells since i was small and i still don't fully understand the impulse. something about finding what the sea leaves behind feels important — like reading a sentence the ocean started and never finished. travel has taken me to a lot of beaches. #Barbados shorelines scattered with whelks and coral fragments. #StJohn coves so quiet you can hear the water thinking. and every time i crouch down to pick something up i feel the same thing: smallness but the good kind. the kind that loosens whatever the week had tightened. the ocean doesn't care about the news cycle and i find that profoundly comforting right now.
alt_text: A sun-warmed hand holding a spiral shell on a white sand beach with shallow turquoise ocean water softly blurred in the background and golden late afternoon light catching the shell's ridges.

title: The Beach Has a Different Answer Every Time I Visit
description: i keep going back to the sea like it owes me something. or maybe like i owe it the visit. travel at its most honest is just this — standing somewhere ancient and admitting that you needed to be humbled. i found a shell on a #TurksAndCaicos beach last year that i carried in my pocket for weeks. i couldn't explain it then and i still can't. but the ocean has a way of giving you exactly the object or the moment or the silence that you didn't know you were looking for. #CaribbeanSea the beach asks nothing of you. after everything the world has been lately i think that's the most generous thing a place can offer.
alt_text: A quiet stretch of empty beach at golden hour with a single large conch shell resting at the waterline sea foam curling around its base and the vast open ocean glowing amber and pink behind it.
